title: World Cup 2026 semifinal schedule: How U.S. viewers can watch France-Spain, England-Argentina
text:
FIFA World

Cup 2026

Ousmane Dembélé heads to the semis, where France next faces Spain as it bids for a third straight finals berth. Alex Slitz / Getty Images

The largest men’s World Cup ever played is approaching the mountaintop. What started with 48 teams has at last narrowed to its final four. Superpower semifinals await.

Just like it did in 2022, France beat Morocco 2-0, this time thanks to goals from dual stars Kylian Mbappé and Ousmane Dembélé. Les Bleus are just one win from a third consecutive World Cup final, and two wins from reclaiming their title. The juggernaut French are still unbeaten in this tournament.

Advertisement

They’re challenged on Tuesday by Spain, a historic stalwart in its own right. La Roja survived the quarterfinal against Belgium, a 2-1 triumph lifted by substitute Mikel Merino in the 88th minute. Spanish goalkeeper Unai Simón lost his clean sheet streak, but the disciplined Spanish squad has conceded one single score across six World Cup matches.

England roared ever closer to it “Coming Home” after topping Norway 2-1 behind Jude Bellingham’s brace. Bellingham’s clutch second goal came three minutes into extra time, and it sealed another inspired three-save performance from Jordan Pickford.

The Three Lions next battle one GOAT contender as Lionel Messi leads his side into Atlanta. Argentina arrives to Wednesday’s matchup after it defeated Switzerland 3-1 in extra time. Julián Alvarez curled a sensational shot into the net and booked La Albiceleste’s semifinal spot. While England tries to break a championship drought that stretches back to 1966, Argentina goes for the first successful title defense since Brazil in 1962.

France and Spain get a rematch of their 2025 Nations League thriller. England and Argentina revisit ghosts and glories of the 1986 “Hand of God” classic. What a semifinal round this should be.

U.S. viewers can tune in to every game of the 2026 World Cup on Fubo in English (stream now) and Spanish (watch here).

All times are ET.
